newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 14.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

The Indonesian armed forces (ABRI) has said it does not have to defend its report of the July 27 riots which differs from the report released last Saturday by the National Commission on Human Rights. The commission reported that five people had died in the riots and 23 were still missing.

Abdurrahaman Wahid, leader of the 35-million strong Moslem organisation Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), has asked for the nation's forgiveness following the burning of churches in east Java on Thursday which resulted in the death of five people. Wahid, who is better known as Gus Dur, admitted that the attacks were mostly carried out by members of NU. According to witnesses, 21 churches were burnt in the violence.

Shares in Indonesian car manufacturer PT Astra International are expected to go above 4,000 rupiah today on speculation that the Nusamba group, controlled by timber tycoon "Bob" Hasan, may make an offer for a stake.
